articles.title: Will AI backlash delay Anthropic IPO? Investors raise doubts
articles.summary: Investors are pushing for a more attractive valuation to commit to the offering, with some ⁠viewing the recently discussed $1.5 trillion valuation as being at the high end of expectations

articles.title: Anthropic may need to cut IPO ambitions as investors balk: report
articles.summary: Anthropic may have to accept a lower valuation than the $1.5 trillion it had been targeting for its stock market debut, after a sharp tech sell-off spooked key investors, the Wall Street Journal reported Thursday. The listing comes amid growing nervousness among investors about the huge sums being poured into AI. Three major investors who plan to take part in the offering told the Journal the valuation would likely need to be lowered, with one saying it could end up closer to $1 trillion.

articles.title: Kospi Slides After US Rout, Triggering Circuit Breaker
articles.summary: Asian stocks slumped after a post-election rout in chipmakers deepened on Wall Street amid growing concern that Democrats will seek tighter regulation of the artificial intelligence industry. Bloomberg's Paul Dobson has the context. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Nasdaq heading for worst day in 18 months as Wall Street sustains widespread losses
articles.summary: Share index slumps 5% amid signs AI industry will face tougher regulation after Democrats’ midterm elections successThe tech-heavy US Nasdaq share index is on track for its worst day in 18 months after slumping by up to 5% on Thursday amid growing signs that the artificial intelligence industry will face tougher regulation after this week’s midterm elections.As Wall Street sustained widespread losses, the Nasdaq composite tumbled into ‘correction territory’ – more than 10% below its recent record high. The index was heading for its biggest one-day fall since Donald Trump announced his ‘liberation day’ tariffs on US trading partners in April 2025. Continue reading...

articles.title: Google extends voluntary buyout offers to employees in several countries
articles.summary: The move comes amid mounting AI spending that has unnerved Wall Street and dented Alphabet's stock price. Microsoft last week offered voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees in an effort to contain costs. Alphabet's workforce has grown steadily in recent quarters, but it has sought to shift resources toward priority areas.

articles.title: Most Venture Capital Is Going To Companies That Are Founded Or Led By Billionaires
articles.summary: More than half of all seed- through growth-stage venture capital raised in the U.S. so far in 2026 went to seven companies founded or led by men who are already billionaires. Together, these companies raised more than $260 billion in equity funding in the first 10 months of the year.

articles.title: Anthropic says revenue surged 1,100% ahead of IPO
articles.summary: Anthropic, one of the world's leading artificial intelligence companies, on Monday reported a more than 1,100 percent surge in quarterly revenue and nearly $900 billion in spending commitments as it counts down to its Wall Street listing later this month. The filing said the company has committed to spend about $895 billion, mostly on computing power, with $70 billion of that due before September 2027.

articles.title: Goldman Sachs pulls AI coding tools from traders and bankers
articles.summary: Goldman Sachs is pulling AI coding tools like Claude Code and GitHub Copilot from traders and bankers, limiting access to engineers only. As recently as July, CIO Marco Argenti publicly praised "vibe coding" by non-technical staff. Now the bank cites "productivity and risk management" as the reason for the reversal.
